extraction.name: SeamlessM4T
extraction.description: SeamlessM4T is a massively multilingual and multimodal machine translation model supporting speech-to-speech, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, text-to-text translation, and automatic speech recognition for up to 100 languages. The work also introduces SeamlessAlign, a multimodal corpus of automatically aligned speech translations.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: 1 million hours of open speech audio data were used to learn self-supervised speech representations. A multimodal corpus of automatically aligned speech translations (SeamlessAlign) totaling 470,000 hours was created by chunking raw audio into overlapping segments, applying speech Language Identification (LID), and projecting speech and text corpora into a common embedding space to mine translation pairs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 4 million hours of raw audio originating from a publicly available repository of crawled web data (approximately 1 million hours in English). Text data relies entirely on the sentence-segmented dataset deployed in NLLB.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio files were chunked into overlapping segments using Voice Activity Detection (VAD) and speech Language Identification (LID). Several possible overlapping splits of each segment were created, leaving the choice of the optimal split to the mining algorithm. The top 400 hours of SeamlessAlign in each of 33 X–eng directions and the top 200 hours in each of 29 eng–X directions based on Sonar alignment scores were used.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio file URLs were deduplicated, downloaded, and resampled at 16KHz. Non-speech data was filtered out with an audio event detection (AED) model. For human-labeled data, special tokens (<silence>, <no-speech>) were removed. Length filtering removed examples exceeding 100 sub-word tokens and pairs with a skewed text-to-audio length ratio exceeding 5 sub-words per second. A toxicity filter removed pairs with toxicity imbalance. Pairs were removed if the utterance was shorter than 0.1s or longer than 50s, or if the text was longer than 250 sub-words, contained >20% emojis, >50% punctuations, or >50% spaces.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For XSTS evaluation, annotators examined source-target audio/text pairs for semantic similarity. Annotators completed monolingual English practice evaluations with score justifications prior to annotating. For MOS evaluation, annotators provided a Likert score (1-5) for clarity of speech, sound quality, and naturalness.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: If 3 annotators had a disagreement of score values of 2 or more, 2 additional annotators evaluated the same item. The median score over annotators of the same audio pair was taken for robustness. Language-level scores were calibrated using the mean score on a cross-lingual calibration set for the crew of annotators evaluating a given language direction.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: NLLB-200-3.3B, Sonar, ETOX, Blaser 2.0, Silero VAD, ECAPA-TDNN
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Personally identifiable information may not be entirely eliminated from the web-crawled data. Gender is represented and analyzed via the HolisticBias dataset.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: SeamlessM4T could augment world-readiness by streamlining multilingual exchange and lowering barriers in cross-lingual communication. It can aid inclusion for those with accessibility needs (e.g., visual impairments) and those whose languages contain multiple writing systems. However, it could also make groups with lower digital literacy vulnerable to misinformation or online scams if misappropriated.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The model overgeneralizes to masculine forms when translating from neutral terms (average preference of ~10%) and shows a lack of robustness when varying gender (~3%). Gender representation analysis reveals an overrepresentation of masculine lexica compared to feminine in the analyzed datasets. ASR performance may vary based on gender, race, accent, or language.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Not intended for long-form translation; translating longer sequences might result in quality degradation. Cannot be used as certified translations. Word list-based toxicity detectors tend to over-detect terms toxic only in specific contexts and rely on precise tokenization. Using ASR before lexical matching tends to lead to false negatives.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Primary intended uses: Research in speech and text translation (ASR, S2ST, S2TT, T2ST, T2TT, TTS). Out-of-scope use cases: Production deployment, domain-specific inputs (medical or legal domains), long-form translation, and certified translations.
